title: Validator Equivocation Attack Solana
text:
Validator Equivocation Attack on Solana

Description:
Equivocation occurs when a validator signs two different blocks for the same
slot, creating a fork. This violates the safety property of Tower BFT consensus.

Attack mechanism:
1. Attacker compromises validator private key
2. Validator signs two conflicting blocks at same slot height
3. Network receives contradictory blocks from same leader
4. Fork detection triggers but resolution takes time
5. Double-spend possible during fork window

Detection indicators:
- duplicate_block_count > 0 in validator metrics
- Same validator pubkey appearing in two fork heads
- Tower BFT violation alerts
- Sudden fork_count increase

Solana Tower BFT protection:
- Validators lock their votes: cannot vote on competing forks
- Lockout exponentially increases with each vote
- Slashing proposed for equivocation (SIMD-0204)
- Current mitigation: social slashing, stake loss

Monitoring:
- solana-gossip spy to watch for duplicate block announcements
- Monitor fork counts via RPC getBlockCommitment
- Track validator vote patterns for anomalies

Impact: Chain halt, double-spend, consensus instability
Severity: Critical — rare but catastrophic
Source: Anza Technical Report, Tower BFT specification
